discovery: Optical detection and coherent control of single electron spins in diamond (NV centres), establishing solid-state quantum sensing
motivation: Wrachtrup first demonstrated optical detection and coherent manipulation of a single electron spin in a solid, the nitrogen-vacancy centre in diamond, operating at room temperature. Building on this, Lukin, Walsworth and Wrachtrup proposed and realised the use of single NV spins as nanoscale magnetometers (2008), combining quantum coherence with atomic-scale spatial resolution. This turned a single quantum system into a reliable measurement instrument now used across physics: imaging magnetism and current flow in 2D materials and superconductors, detecting nuclear spins from nanoscale volumes, mapping neuronal and biological fields, and probing matter at megabar pressures inside diamond anvil cells. The work also opened the way to spin-photon entanglement and loophole-free Bell tests with solid-state spins. It is a rare example where foundational control of individual quanta has given the wider scientific community an entirely new, quantitative measurement capability.
